item.title: Shark Graveyard Found in Egyptian Desert
item.description:
Shark Graveyard Found in Egyptian Desert

The Western Desert of Egypt is a place of wind and phosphate, not of surf. About 80 million years ago it was a shallow inland sea. Paleontologists led by Cairo University’s Tarek Yassin have now pulled 14 fossil shark teeth from phosphate beds on the Abu-Tartur Plateau, and those teeth are enough to redraw a local roster of Cretaceous hunters. The find is being called a shark “graveyard,” with the scare quotes doing honest work. It is not a single pile of animals that died together. It is a seafloor archive from a mixed, nutrient-rich Tethys margin, later lifted into desert as the sea retreated.
